observations.statement: Centered progression sums split large moduli by the pointwise logarithmic bound and small moduli by fixed-field Siegel–Walfisz. The intersection with the cyclotomic field is exactly the maximal abelian subfield already contained by W, so the two main terms cancel. Nonunit residue classes contribute only exceptional primes.

Gaussian norm transfer assumes total equidistribution on the original one-parameter orbit. Quadratic coefficient extrapolation clears bounded integer leading coefficients in descending order; the small horizontal-character obstruction uses a sufficiently long initial interval and metric Lipschitz control. These are local arguments supplementing the published quantitative Leibman theorem.

The norm-transfer proof counts every nonzero ideal by four Gaussian generators, splits horizontal rows into constant-character blocks and progression classes, and bounds annulus endpoints uniformly even for short intervals. Quadratic pullback uses the stretched filtration and quantitative Leibman. Product transfer requires equidistribution of the entire product orbit, which does not follow merely from mean-zero factors.

Ideal norm multiplicities are bounded by divisor moments and disk counting. Exact ideal convolution gives Vaughan decomposition with stated cutoffs and no endpoint error, using complete multiplicativity of the zero-extended ray character.

Quantitative extraction passes from ideals to integer norm parameters using second moments. Two Cauchy–Schwarz steps retain all conjugates and remove character/Mobius coefficients in Type II. Product cutoffs remain in the test function, leaving rectangular sums; progression intersections are a single class modulo a divisor of q.

Integer-parameter recombination applies quantitative Leibman after failure on a long progression. It explicitly removes large shifts with denominator clearing, pigeonholes bounded horizontal characters, handles small Type I scales separately, and invokes the published recurrence lemma at arbitrary arc centers for Type II. It does not replace differences of powers by powers of differences.

The minor-arc bound combines extraction, norm transfer and recombination with explicit exponent inequalities. It checks modulus/rationality/lower-parameter conditions, extends shell estimates over scales, then treats tiny delta by monotonicity or singleton progressions. Dependence of the saving exponent is on dimension and degree, while the fixed ray modulus enters constants.
